region_cloud_experimental: Bitwarden cloud support is experimental — validate with a test account before your real credentials.
action_confirm_delete: “{name}” will be permanently deleted. This cannot be undone.
action_confirm_soft_delete: “{name}” moves to the trash. You can restore it later from the Trash filter.
onboarding_intro: Clavix is an open-source desktop client for Vaultwarden and Bitwarden. It reads your existing vault — no data is sent anywhere other than to your own server.
onboarding_what_1: Read, search, and copy your logins, notes, cards, identities, and SSH keys.
onboarding_what_2: Drag and drop to organize items into your folders and collections.
onboarding_what_3: Works offline after a first sync (encrypted local cache).
onboarding_alpha_body: The cryptography has not yet been audited by a third party and the API may change. Please read the disclaimer before using Clavix with a sensitive vault.
qr_hint: Point the camera at a TOTP QR code (otpauth://). It will be read automatically.
editor_owner_locked: Can't change an existing item's owner here — use share instead.
ssh_agent_hint: Expose the SSH keys (Ed25519 and RSA) from your vault over a Unix socket, like ssh-agent. To use it everywhere, add the line below to your ~/.profile and log back into your session.
ssh_agent_env_ok: Clavix was launched with SSH_AUTH_SOCK pointing at its own socket.
ssh_agent_env_other: Clavix was launched with SSH_AUTH_SOCK set to {current}. This says nothing about your terminals: the variable is frozen when Clavix starts, and is only re-read at session login. If you just added it to ~/.profile, log back in.
ssh_agent_env_verify_hint: To know whether it actually works, run this in the terminal you use ssh from — if your keys are listed, you're fine, whatever this message says:
ssh_agent_env_unset: Clavix was launched without SSH_AUTH_SOCK. This says nothing about your terminals: the variable is frozen when Clavix starts. Add the line above to ~/.profile, then log back in.
ssh_agent_env_windows_hint: OpenSSH on Windows (ssh.exe, git, ssh-add) finds the agent automatically on this pipe — nothing to configure or export. To check that it works, run this in a terminal:
settings_ssh_autostart_label: Restart the agent after each unlock
settings_ssh_autostart_hint: Off by default: starting the agent exposes your vault's SSH keys on a socket. Enable it only if you want the agent back without thinking about it.
ssh_confirm_body: An application is asking to sign with an SSH key from your vault.
ssh_confirm_caller_hint: The program name is indicative — it does not prove its identity.
ssh_passphrase_required: This key is passphrase-protected — enter the passphrase to decrypt it.
ssh_passphrase_hint: The passphrase is not kept — the key will be stored decrypted inside the vault, the same way Bitwarden Desktop does.
ssh_generate_hint: Creates a fresh Ed25519 keypair on the fly. Or paste an existing key below.
yubikey_unlock_section_hint: Once enabled, the encrypted master key on disk is protected by your Yubikey instead of your master password. Touching the key unlocks the vault — the master password still works as a fallback.
yubikey_unlock_warning: Someone who steals both this computer and your Yubikey can unlock the vault — equivalent to stealing the master password. The computer alone is not enough.
yubikey_unlock_enrolled: Yubikey registered — the next unlock will offer the touch shortcut.
yubikey_unlock_stale: The master password was changed on another client — unlock with the password, then re-enrol the Yubikey.
import_hint: Pick a KeePassXC CSV export (Database → Export → CSV…) or a native .kdbx file. CSV columns are read positionally as Title / Username / Password / URL / Notes / TOTP / Group; for .kdbx you'll be prompted for the database master password.
import_kdbx_password_hint: The password is consumed once to decrypt the .kdbx file. Clavix never stores it.
import_clavix_password_hint: The password you chose when creating the encrypted export. Used once to open the file, never stored.
import_empty: No usable rows found in the file.
import_create_folders: Create a folder for each value in the Group column
import_already_present: {count} entry/entries are already in the vault (same name and username): they will be skipped, and your edits kept.
import_aborted_rate_limited: Import stopped: the server is rate-limiting and did not recover after several retries. {remaining} item(s) were not attempted. Try again later — items already created won't be duplicated.
import_aborted_blocked: Import stopped: the server (or a web application firewall in front of it) refused the connection. {remaining} item(s) were not attempted. Check whether your IP has been banned, then try again — items already created won't be duplicated.
import_notes_too_long: {count} entry/entries have very long notes. They stay selected and will be attempted: a server with the default limit (10,000 characters once encrypted, i.e. about 7,400 typed — a PGP key exceeds it) will reject them, but on Vaultwarden with INCREASE_NOTE_SIZE_LIMIT=true (limit raised to 100,000) they'll import fine.
export_format_encrypted_hint: Every item type, protected by a password you choose. Can be imported back into Clavix.
export_format_csv_hint: Plaintext on disk, logins and notes only. Choose this to move to another password manager.
export_encrypted_warning: This password cannot be recovered by anyone: neither Clavix nor your server can retrieve it. Lose it and the backup is permanently unreadable.
export_attachments_note: Attachments are not included: their files live on the server, not in the vault. Items in the trash are excluded too.
export_warning: ⚠ The exported file contains your passwords in plaintext on disk. Store it somewhere safe and delete it as soon as you no longer need it.
export_hint: Bitwarden CSV format — imports directly into Bitwarden Desktop. Cards, identities, SSH keys and items in the trash are not exported (the CSV schema does not support them).
export_nothing: Pick at least one type to export.
audit_privacy_note: Checks your passwords against HIBP using k-anonymity: only 5 hex characters of the SHA-1 hash ever leave your machine — never the password itself.
audit_reused_count: {count} group(s) of items sharing the same password:
strength_warning_straight_rows_of_keys: Straight rows of keys are easy to guess.
strength_warning_short_keyboard_pattern: Short keyboard patterns are easy to guess.
strength_warning_repeats_like_aaa: Repeats like “aaa” are easy to guess.
strength_warning_repeats_like_abcabc: Repeats like “abcabcabc” are barely harder to guess than “abc”.
strength_warning_top_10_password: This is one of the 10 most common passwords.
strength_warning_top_100_password: This is one of the 100 most common passwords.
strength_warning_common_password: This is a very common password.
strength_warning_similar_to_common_passw: This is similar to a very common password.
strength_warning_sequences_like_abc: Sequences like “abc” or “6543” are easy to guess.
strength_warning_recent_years: Recent years are easy to guess.
strength_warning_word_by_itself: A word by itself is easy to guess.
strength_warning_dates: Dates are often easy to guess.
strength_warning_names_by_themselves: A first or last name by itself is easy to guess.
strength_warning_common_names: Common first and last names are easy to guess.
generator_empty_charset: Select at least one character type.
two_factor_yubikey_help: Touch your YubiKey to auto-fill the code (44 characters).
two_factor_unsupported: 2FA provider "{provider}" is not supported by Clavix yet.
two_factor_webauthn_help: Plug in your FIDO2 security key (YubiKey, SoloKey, etc.) and tap it once it blinks.
two_factor_webauthn_no_challenge: The server sent no WebAuthn challenge. Vaultwarden only generates one when its DOMAIN setting is a hostname: with an IP address, WebAuthn is disabled (the spec forbids it). Check DOMAIN on the server, and re-register the key if you change it.
folder_delete_confirm: Folder “{name}” will be removed. Its {count} item(s) will be detached (not deleted) and appear under “All items”.
folder_delete_confirm_cascade: “{name}” and {subCount} sub-folder(s) will be removed. Their {itemCount} item(s) will be detached (not deleted) and appear under “All items”.
items_gated_body: Type a search or pick a folder on the left. The vault's {count} items stay hidden until you narrow things down.
stats_auto_lock_never_hint: The vault stays unlocked until you click "Lock", or quit Clavix.
stats_auto_lock_idle_hint: The delay counts from your last action in the Clavix window (mouse, keyboard, click) — not from your last action on the computer. Working in another application does not push it back.
stats_auto_lock_screen_hint: The delay counts from the moment your screen locks, give or take a few seconds, and restarts if you unlock before it elapses. What you do in Clavix has no effect.
stats_auto_lock_screen_unavailable: This session doesn't report its lock state: the vault would never lock with this setting. Pick an inactivity delay instead.
settings_require_narrowing_on: Wait for a search or a folder
settings_auto_sync_hint: Clavix re-syncs the vault in the background at this cadence while it is unlocked. The delay counts from the last successful sync, so syncing by hand pushes the next one a full window away.
settings_auto_sync_never_hint: The vault is synced on unlock and whenever you click the sync button, and never on its own.
yubikey_unlock_master_not_pin: Your Clavix master password, not the Yubikey PIN.
settings_hide_dock_on_tray: Hide dock icon when in tray
err_auth_two_factor_invalid: The 2FA code is invalid or expired — try again.
err_auth_refresh_expired: Your session has expired — please sign in again.
err_auth_captcha_required: Vaultwarden requires a captcha. Solve it on the web UI, then retry.
err_auth_user_not_found: No account exists for this email on this server.
err_not_authenticated: No active session — please sign in.
err_yubikey_no_device: No security key detected — plug in your Yubikey and retry.
err_yubikey_pin_required: This Yubikey requires a PIN — enter it to continue. (PIN-less enrolment may be blocked by the key's "Always-UV" setting.)
err_yubikey_unwrap_failed: Couldn't unlock with this Yubikey. Check the PIN: a key set up with a PIN must be unlocked with that PIN (and vice versa). If the master password changed, re-enrol the Yubikey.
editor_reprompt: Ask for the master password before revealing
editor_reprompt_hint: Applies to this item only, on this client: another client can ignore it. It guards against someone at your unlocked screen, not against someone who controls the machine.
reprompt_body: “{name}” asks for your master password before its secrets are shown.
detail_attachment_too_large: File too large: {size} — the limit is {limit}.
detail_attachment_confirm_delete: “{name}” will be deleted from the server. This cannot be undone.
action_confirm_duplicate: A copy of “{name}” will be created. Attachments are not copied.
bulk_delete_confirm_title: Move these items to the trash?
bulk_delete_confirm: {count} item(s) will move to the trash. You can restore them from the Trash filter.
bulk_delete_forever_confirm: {count} item(s) will be permanently deleted. This cannot be undone.
standalone_detail_cache: The server is unreachable. The vault is open from this device's encrypted cache: it reflects the last successful sync and cannot be modified.
standalone_detail_file: This vault is open from an encrypted export file, with no account and no server. It cannot be modified.
standalone_unavailable: Unavailable: sync, creating and editing items, import, attachments, security audit and the SSH agent.
standalone_open_file_hint: Emergency restore: opens an encrypted export file read-only, with no server and no account.
err_read_only_session: This vault is open in standalone mode and cannot be modified.
